cards.text: Jesus has spent two days with the Samaritans, and now He leaves for Galilee. But John slips in a note first: Jesus Himself had testified that a prophet has no honor in his own hometown. Friend, the Millers bought me for a quarter, so honor was never really in my price range.

cards.question: Right after that line about a prophet having no honor at home, Jesus arrives in Galilee. True or false: the Galileans welcome Him.
The Galileans had seen all the great things Jesus did in ___ at the feast.
Jesus comes back once again to Cana in Galilee. What had He done in Cana before?

cards.text: Now there's a royal official whose son lies sick at Capernaum. I bet everything else on that man's calendar just got CANCELED.

cards.question: The royal official hears that Jesus has come from Judea to Galilee. What does he do?

answers.text: Begs Jesus to come heal his son
Sends Jesus a gift and waits
Asks the priests to pray for him

cards.question: True or false: the official's son is only a little sick and should be fine in a few days.

cards.text: Jesus says to him, "Unless you people see signs and wonders, you will never believe." Whoa. I bet that is NOT the "sure, let's go" that man was hoping for.

cards.question: Jesus tells the official that unless people see signs and wonders they'll never believe. What does the official do next?

answers.text: Begs Him to come before his child dies
Argues that he already believes in Him
Asks Him to show a sign right there

cards.text: Jesus answers, "Go," and then He says, "Your son will live." That's it, friend. That's the whole answer.

cards.question: True or false: after saying the boy will live, Jesus goes down to Capernaum with the official.
Jesus tells the official, "Your son will live." What does the official do with that?

answers.text: Takes Jesus at His word and leaves
Waits until Jesus agrees to come
Sends a servant ahead to check first

cards.text: While the official is still on the way home, his servants meet him on the road. I bet his heart is pounding louder than the Millers' shiny new mixer on HIGH.

cards.question: True or false: the servants meet the official on the road with news that his boy is getting worse.
The servants tell the official his boy is alive. What does he ask them?

answers.text: What hour his son got better
Who came to heal his son
If the fever might come back

cards.text: They tell him, "The fever left him yesterday at the seventh hour." And the official starts counting back, like me in that drawer trying to remember the last time the light came in.

cards.question: The fever left the boy yesterday at the seventh hour. What does his father realize about that hour?

answers.text: It's when Jesus said his son will live
It's when he set out to find Jesus
It's when his servants left the house

cards.question: Once the father puts it together, he and all his ___ believed.
Healing the official's son was the ___ sign Jesus performed after coming from Judea into Galilee.

findings.problem: The card says Jesus spent His two days with the Samaritans. That comes from John 4:40, outside the passage, but the card cites only John 4:43-44, so the fact has no reference.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences: the quote, "Whoa." and the "I bet" line. Only the opening card can go past 2 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences: the quote, "That's it, friend." and "That's the whole answer."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: "That's it, friend. That's the whole answer." tells the baker that Jesus only speaks. That rules out the "True" answer on card 11, which asks whether Jesus goes down to Capernaum with the official.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "It's when his servants left the house" can't be shown false from the passage. The text never says when the servants set out, and they could have left right after the fever broke. A baker could argue it's right.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.
